questions.question: Thermogenin (uncoupling protein 1, UCP1) increases the proton permeability of the inner mitochondrial membrane in brown adipose tissue. What is the primary direct physiological consequence of UCP1 activation?
options: Increased rate of ATP synthesis via ATP synthase
Immediate shutdown of the citric acid cycle due to elevated ATP/ADP ratios
Inhibition of fatty acid oxidation in the mitochondrial matrix
Dissipation of the proton motive force as heat without generating ATP

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the genome replication strategy of viruses belonging to Group VI in the Baltimore classification system (e.g., Retroviridae)?
options: Single-stranded (+ sense) RNA converted into double-stranded DNA by viral reverse transcriptase prior to integration into the host genome
Double-stranded DNA converted into an RNA intermediate that is reverse-transcribed back to DNA inside newly assembled capsids
Negative-sense single-stranded RNA transcribed directly into mRNA by host RNA polymerase II
Double-stranded RNA unwound by viral helicase to serve directly as translation templates

questions.question: In the canonical Wnt signaling pathway, what intracellular event occurs when a Wnt ligand binds to the Frizzled/LRP receptor complex?
options: Phosphorylation of beta-catenin by GSK-3beta, triggering its rapid degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway
Inhibition of the beta-catenin destruction complex, allowing unphosphorylated beta-catenin to accumulate and translocate to the nucleus
Cleavage of the Frizzled intracellular domain by gamma-secretase, which translocates to act directly as a transcription factor
Direct phosphorylation and activation of STAT transcription factors by inherent receptor tyrosine kinase activity

questions.question: How does the long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) product of the XIST gene initiate transcriptional silencing during mammalian X-chromosome inactivation?
options: It functions as a microRNA precursor that selectively degrades mRNAs transcribed from the targeted X chromosome
It acts in trans to degrade basal transcription factors required for RNA polymerase II binding on autosomal chromosomes
It coats the chosen X chromosome in cis and recruits chromatin-modifying complexes that induce repressive histone modifications
It cleaves DNA at specific promoter regions along the inactive X chromosome via intrinsic ribozyme activity

questions.question: Trypsinogen is a zymogen secreted by the exocrine pancreas. Which enzyme at the duodenal brush border initiates the cleavage cascade that converts trypsinogen into active trypsin?
options: Pepsin
Carboxypeptidase A
Chymotrypsin
Enteropeptidase
